introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Further Mathematics 3 (0775), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2026. Duration: Two and a Half Hours.**

Answer ALL questions. For your guidance the approximate mark allocation for parts of each question is indicated in brackets. Mathematical formulae and tables, published by the Board, and noiseless non-programmable electronic calculators are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage.
incertitudes: Question 1 (i) : le sujet imprime seulement l'intensité (7 N) et la droite d'action de F3, sans en donner le sens. Le corrigé retient le sens du vecteur directeur écrit dans l'équation de la droite, F3 = 6i + 3j + 2k. Le résultat pour le sens opposé est donné en remarque (F4 = -5i + 4j - 5k, G = -10i - 5j + 6k).
Question 1 (iii) : la droite d'action de F3 passe aussi par le point de concours C de F1 et F2 (pour mu = -1), ce que le sujet ne dit pas ; le corrigé s'en sert pour vérifier le moment G.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find $\mathbf{F}_3$ in terms of $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{k}$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The line of action of $\mathbf{F}_3$ is parallel to the direction vector $\mathbf{d} = 6\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$, whose magnitude is

$$
|\mathbf{d}| = \sqrt{6^2 + 3^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{49} = 7.
$$

A force of magnitude $7\ \mathrm{N}$ along $\mathbf{d}$ is $7$ times the unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{d}} = \dfrac{\mathbf{d}}{7}$:

$$
\mathbf{F}_3 = 7\cdot\frac{6\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}}{7} = (6\mathbf{i} + 3\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}.
$$

The statement gives the line but not the sense of the force; the sense of the direction vector written in the equation of the line is taken. (If $\mathbf{F}_3$ acted in the opposite sense, it would be $-6\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ are concurrent and find the position vector $\overrightarrow{OC}$ of their point of concurrence. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two lines in space are concurrent when they intersect. The lines of action are

$$
\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ -3 \\ -3 \end{pmatrix} + \lambda\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad
\mathbf{r} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} + \nu\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Equate the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{i}: &\quad 3 - \lambda = 3 + 2\nu \\
\mathbf{j}: &\quad -3 + 3\lambda = 2 + 4\nu \\
\mathbf{k}: &\quad -3 + \lambda = -4 - 4\nu
\end{aligned}
$$

The first equation gives $\lambda = -2\nu$. Substituting in the second: $-3 - 6\nu = 2 + 4\nu$, so $\nu = -\dfrac12$ and $\lambda = 1$.

Check in the third equation: left side $-3 + 1 = -2$; right side $-4 - 4\left(-\tfrac12\right) = -2$. The three equations are consistent, so the lines intersect: $\mathbf{F}_1$ and $\mathbf{F}_2$ are concurrent.

Substituting $\lambda = 1$ in the first line:

$$
\overrightarrow{OC} = (3 - 1)\mathbf{i} + (-3 + 3)\mathbf{j} + (-3 + 1)\mathbf{k} = (2\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}.
$$

(The second line with $\nu = -\tfrac12$ gives the same point: $3 - 1,\ 2 - 2,\ -4 + 2$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
This system of three forces is equivalent to a fourth force $\mathbf{F}_4$ acting through the point with position vector $(3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{m}$, together with a couple $\mathbf{G}$.

Find $\mathbf{F}_4$ and $\mathbf{G}$. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**The force $\mathbf{F}_4$** is the resultant of the three forces:

$$
\mathbf{F}_4 = \mathbf{F}_1 + \mathbf{F}_2 + \mathbf{F}_3 = (-1 + 2 + 6)\mathbf{i} + (3 + 4 + 3)\mathbf{j} + (1 - 4 + 2)\mathbf{k} = (7\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N}.
$$

**The couple $\mathbf{G}$** is the sum of the moments of the three forces about the point $P(3, -2, -2)$ through which $\mathbf{F}_4$ acts (the moment of $\mathbf{F}_4$ about its own point of action is zero). For a force $\mathbf{F}$ acting through a point $A$, the moment about $P$ is $\overrightarrow{PA}\times\mathbf{F}$.

$$
\mathbf{G}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ -1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}\times\begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad
\mathbf{G}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 \\ 4 \\ -2 \end{pmatrix}\times\begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ -4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} -8 \\ -4 \\ -8 \end{pmatrix},
$$

and, for $\mathbf{F}_3$ (which acts through the point $(8, 3, 0)$ of its line, $\overrightarrow{PA} = 5\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$):

$$
\mathbf{G}_3 = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ 5 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}\times\begin{pmatrix} 6 \\ 3 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \\ -15 \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Adding:

$$
\mathbf{G} = \mathbf{G}_1 + \mathbf{G}_2 + \mathbf{G}_3 = (-2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} - 24\mathbf{k})\ \mathrm{N\,m}.
$$

**Check.** The line of $\mathbf{F}_3$ also passes through $C(2, 0, -2)$ (take $\mu = -1$), so the three forces are concurrent at $C$ and their moment about $P$ is that of $\mathbf{F}_4$ placed at $C$: $\overrightarrow{PC}\times\mathbf{F}_4 = (-\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j})\times(7\mathbf{i} + 10\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}) = -2\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j} - 24\mathbf{k}$, the same result.

**Remark.** If $\mathbf{F}_3$ were taken in the opposite sense, $-6\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k}$, the same method would give $\mathbf{F}_4 = -5\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} - 5\mathbf{k}$ and $\mathbf{G} = -10\mathbf{i} - 5\mathbf{j} + 6\mathbf{k}$.
